cards.canonical_statement: For any commutative ring R and R-module M, M is Noetherian if and only if every submodule of M is finitely generated.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the equivalence between the ascending chain condition and finite generation of all submodules.
sketch_steps: Fix the ring and module without any finiteness assumption.
Use the equivalence between the ascending chain condition and finite generation of all submodules.
The forward direction applies Noetherianity to an arbitrary submodule.
The reverse direction reconstructs Noetherianity from this universal finite-generation condition.

cards.canonical_statement: For any commutative ring R, R-module M and submodule U, M is Noetherian if and only if both U and M/U are Noetherian.
cards.proof_strategy: Noetherian modules pass the chain condition to submodules and quotients.
sketch_steps: Fix an arbitrary submodule U of M.
Noetherian modules pass the chain condition to submodules and quotients.
For the converse, use the exact sequence U → M → M/U.
Combine the two chain conditions to obtain the condition on the middle module.

cards.canonical_statement: For any commutative ring R, the product of two Noetherian R-modules is Noetherian.
cards.proof_strategy: Embed the first factor and project onto the second.
sketch_steps: Fix the two modules with their chain conditions.
Embed the first factor and project onto the second.
This produces an exact sequence with the two factors as endpoints.
Closure under extensions gives the chain condition on their product.

cards.proof_strategy: Thus localization of the zero submodule contains only zero.

Every localized element has a numerator in M.
Hence localization of the whole submodule is the whole localized module.
